opportunities.title: Q3 Was Crypto's Most Expensive Quarter for Security Ever — And the Bitget Hack Alone Was a Third of It
opportunities.why_now: Bitget's $388M breach pushed Q3 losses past $1.26B, and Chainalysis just published the AI forensics trail tying it to North Korea, giving a full data-plus-narrative hook.
opportunities.angle: Data-led postmortem: break down the $1.26B by vector (bridge, custody, DeFi), overlay the Chainalysis AI tracing methodology, end with what 'priced in' means for exchanges still running centralized hot wallets.

opportunities.title: NEAR Intents Got Its $3.8M Back With a 48-Hour Ultimatum. That's Not Recovery — That's Hostage Negotiation
opportunities.why_now: The full arc just closed in 48 hours: exploit, identification, ultimatum, full recovery — a tidy case study in the new 'negotiate with your hacker' playbook.
opportunities.angle: Skeptical breakdown of white-hat-adjacent extortion-as-incident-response: what precedent this sets, why it only works when the protocol can identify the attacker, and why most victims never get this luxury.

opportunities.title: Drift's Exploit Victims Just Got Checks for 1% of What They Lost. This Is What 'We're Making Users Whole' Actually Means
opportunities.why_now: Drift opened recovery claims this week with initial payouts just over 1% of losses, a concrete number that exposes the gap between PR language and reality.
opportunities.angle: Myth-busting explainer using Drift as Exhibit A: track the language protocols use after hacks ('made whole,' 'recovery fund') against the actual payout math, with a running tally of other unresolved DeFi exploits.

opportunities.title: Zano's Exploiter Minted a Quadrillion Fake Tokens Before Anyone Noticed. The Rollback Fixed the Ledger, Not the Trust
opportunities.why_now: A quadrillion-unit overmint is a jaw-dropping number that happened just days ago and forced a full chain rollback — rare enough to be a standalone security case study.
opportunities.angle: Technical-but-readable breakdown of how the mint bug worked, why rollbacks are the nuclear option, and what it says about audit coverage on smaller L1s nobody's watching.

opportunities.title: BitGo's CEO Says Clarity's Collapse Could Be Worse Than Lehman. He's Describing Plumbing Risk, Not Headline Risk
opportunities.why_now: A regulated custodian CEO invoking Lehman this week is a rare moment where 'security-led' crypto commentary crosses into traditional systemic-risk language worth dissecting.
opportunities.angle: Op-ed translating the custody/market-structure jargon into plain stakes: what actually breaks if Clarity's framework fails, who's exposed, and why this reads like every pre-crisis warning that got ignored.
